questions.q: Propanenitrile (CH₃CH₂C≡N) is reduced with sodium and ethanol. The product is:
questions.explain: Four hydrogen atoms add across C≡N, and the nitrile carbon becomes the CH₂ bonded to nitrogen, giving CH₃CH₂CH₂NH₂. No carbon is lost.

questions.q: Methyl isocyanide, CH₃–N≡C, is fully reduced. The product is:
questions.explain: In an isocyanide the carbon ends up on nitrogen as a methyl group, so a secondary amine R–NH–CH₃ forms. The isomeric nitrile CH₃C≡N would give the primary amine ethanamine.

questions.q: Which reagent does NOT convert R–C≡N into the primary amine R–CH₂–NH₂?
questions.explain: SnCl₂/HCl followed by hydrolysis is the Stephen reduction, which stops at the aldehyde R–CHO. The other three all give the same primary amine.

questions.q: CH₃CH₂Cl →(KCN)→ A →(Na, C₂H₅OH)→ B. Compared with chloroethane, B is:
options: Ethanamine, with the same number of carbons
questions.explain: Cyanide adds one carbon to give propanenitrile, and Mendius reduction keeps every carbon, so B is propan-1-amine. This is an ascent of the amine series; Hofmann bromamide degradation goes the other way.
